newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 110-120 bcf in wkly AGA.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 110-120 bcf in wkly AGA.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 110-120 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged widely from 40 bcf to 175 bcf for the week ended January 10.

"We started the week warm, then it grew dramatically colder. We're undoubtedly going to widen the surplus to last year," said one Texas-based trader, adding the storage scenario was growing more bearish.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by 197 bcf. A draw today in the expected range would widen the surplus to last year to about 150 bcf. In 1996, eastern storage fell by 127 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 59 bcf and western stocks by 11 bcf.

In last report, overall stocks fell by 15 bcf, well-below expectations, and moved to a 69 bcf surplus to last year, the first year-on-year surplus in more than a year. The four week average drawdown is 82 bcf.

While producing and consuming region west inventories continued to lag 1996 levels, stocks in the critical eastern region, which fell in last report by just 26 bcf, were 211 bcf, or almost 20 percent, above year-ago.
